slides.teacher_cue: Three more suffixes. -ing marks ongoing action: run→running (double consonant), swim→swimming, hope→hoping (drop the e). -er marks comparative: fast→faster, big→bigger (double), happy→happier (y→i). -est marks superlative: fast→fastest, big→biggest, happy→happiest. Key spelling rules: double the final consonant before a vowel suffix if the vowel is short (run→running, big→bigger). Drop the silent e before a vowel suffix (hope→hoping, late→later).
slides.expected_response: Students apply the -ing/-er/-est spelling rules correctly.
slides.correction_move: Model: run + ing — short vowel, double n — running. hope + ing — drop e — hoping. big + er — short vowel, double g — bigger. Students apply the rules to new words.
slides.observation_note: Watch for students forgetting to double the consonant or failing to drop the e.

slides.teacher_cue: Say the new focus, then connect suffixes to one strong word from today.

slides.correction_move: Model the focus once, then have students echo and use it in a known word.
slides.observation_note: Listen for whether students can carry the focus from isolation into a real word.
